operations.title: 1246 — All Five-Cycle Candidate Simplex Terms Have One Determinant Weight
operations.body: Every one of the 180 compatible five-cycle denominator bases has determinant magnitude 32=2^5. Triangle and square replications give 2^3 and 2^4. Hence oriented candidate simplex weights are uniform, reducing the missing canonical-form data to a global normalization plus a signed-chain triangulation proof.

operations.title: Benincasa reports uniform five-cycle simplex determinant weights
operations.body: Entry 1246 sharpens the source-completeness gate. Exact determinants of all 180 full denominator normal matrices have |det|=32=2^5; lower-arity replication gives 8 and 16. After orientation correction all candidate simplex terms have one common weight. What remains is a signed-chain triangulation test (internal-face cancellation and unit boundary multiplicity), not reconstruction of 180 coefficients.
